title: Bug by Tracy Letts on Broadway #bugbroadway #carriecoon #namirsmallwo...
transcript: I just saw my last Broadway show of the year, starring Carrie Coon and Namir Smallwood. It's called Bug by Tracy Letts and it was amazing. The play is actually from 1996 but this is the first time it's been on Broadway. Basically, Carrie Coon plays this waitress who's living in this motel in Oklahoma, she meets this man named Peter and over the course of the play she kind of takes on his paranoias. As you might expect from the title, a big component of these paranoias is bugs, but there's also some government conspiracy theory stuff that's pretty wild too. I thought this play was really really interesting as a character study specifically. And I won't give too much away, but it's just really interesting and disturbing how far off the deep end they go. I thought the direction by David Cromer was quite strong — very naturalistic and kind of slow moving at first, but that lays a very solid groundwork and then makes it all the more impactful when things accelerate and then really go off the rails. Above all else though, I just thought Carrie Coon and Namir Smallwood were both amazing, like super, super captivating performances and then especially together, they just have really, really great chemistry. I think they both have such a fearlessness in their performances that really takes this already interesting play just to that next level that's just like “wow.” I'm gonna be thinking about their performances for quite some time, and I hope they both secure Tony nominations too. Bug is still in previews on Broadway, but if it opens to the reception that I hope it does, this could become a very hot ticket. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
